<reason>CON framed the decisive distinction early (disclosure of your own price vs. compelled steering to a rival) and held it through every round. PRO's best precedent (pharmacist generic substitution) was neutralized as same-counter substitution, and under pressure PRO conceded no law compels rival-price display and then relocated the anchor to the app's own pickup total. CON exploited that pivot cleanly: the word "independent" dropped out of PRO's case, leaving either the status quo pickup toggle (redundant with CON's all-in pricing alternative) or an unverifiable rival comparison (unworkable). PRO's closing effectively granted the independent-price point and defended a narrower motion, and PRO never answered the restaurant-squeeze mechanism beyond "it already happens." CON's closing dilemma made the vote easy; PRO's late claim that customers "never learn pickup existed" was undercut by CON's unanswered point that the toggle is already on every listing.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's A2 in Rebuttal 2 ([B4.3]-[B4.4]): tracing how PRO's answer to the anchor question shifted from the restaurant's menu price to "the app's own listed pickup total," then showing that this workable version is the status quo plus a phone number—stripping the motion of its distinctive "independent" content. This set up the closing dilemma that decided the round.</best_rebuttal>
